Save a ggplot (or other grid object) with ggsaveR enhancements

Source: R/ggsave.R
ggsave.Rd

A drop-in replacement for ggplot2::ggsave(). Called without any ggsaveR.* options set, it behaves like the original. Setting options switches on extra behaviour for every ggsave() call in a script: saving to several formats at once, protecting existing files, and embedding metadata in PNG files.

Usage

ggsave(filename, plot = last_plot(), device = NULL, ..., guard = FALSE)

Arguments

filename

File name to create on disk.

plot

Plot to save, defaults to the last plot displayed.

device

Device to use: NULL (guess from the extension of filename), a device name such as "png", a character vector of device names, or a device function. See ggplot2::ggsave(). Ignored when the ggsaveR.formats option is set.

...

Other arguments passed on to ggplot2::ggsave(), such as width, height, units, dpi, scale or bg.

guard

If TRUE, all ggsaveR enhancements are bypassed and the call is forwarded unchanged to ggplot2::ggsave().

Value

Invisibly, a character vector with the paths of the files created.

Options

All enhancements are controlled with options(); see ggsaveR-package for the full reference.

  • ggsaveR.formats: save every plot in several formats and sizes. Either a character vector of devices (c("png", "pdf")) or a list of lists, each with a device and any other ggsave() arguments (list(device = "png", width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300)). The extension of filename is replaced, and the device argument is ignored. Settings in a format take precedence over arguments given in the call.

  • ggsaveR.overwrite_action: what to do when a file already exists: "overwrite" (default), "stop" (error, before anything is written) or "unique" (save as plot-1.png, plot-2.png, ...; all formats of one call share the same suffix).

  • ggsaveR.embed_data: if TRUE, embed the plot object, its data, the call and the session info in PNG files. Read them back with read_ggsaveR_data(). ggsaveR.embed_metadata selects which parts.

  • ggsaveR.creator: a string stored as the Author of PNG files.

Differences from ggplot2

  • device may be a character vector, in which case one file is written per device and the extension of filename is replaced.

  • If filename has no extension and device is a single string, the device is appended as the extension.

  • A character vector of saved paths is returned (invisibly), rather than the single filename.

Embedded data and privacy

With ggsaveR.embed_data = TRUE the PNG contains the raw data behind the plot (all columns, not only the plotted ones) and, for plots built inside a function, every object in that function's environment. Do not share such files if the data are sensitive, and expect larger files. Use ggsaveR.embed_metadata to embed less, or guard = TRUE to skip a single plot.

See also

read_ggsaveR_data() to read embedded data back, ggsaveR-package for the options.

Examples

library(ggplot2)
p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt)) + geom_point()
out <- file.path(tempdir(), "mtcars.png")

# Works like ggplot2::ggsave()
ggsave(out, p, width = 5, height = 4)

# Save every plot as both PNG and PDF, and never overwrite
old <- options(
  ggsaveR.formats = c("png", "pdf"),
  ggsaveR.overwrite_action = "unique"
)
ggsave(out, p, width = 5, height = 4)
#> File exists. Saving to mtcars-1.png, mtcars-1.pdf instead.

# Bypass the options for one call
ggsave(out, p, width = 5, height = 4, guard = TRUE)

options(old)
